solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Head of recruitment is indeed a bigot

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of recruitment is used
the word indeed is split as in deed, so the little word is placed inside the act

parts.note: a deed is an act
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recruiter's boss is exposed as prejudiced.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'indeed' as an emphatic word; the wordplay splits it into 'in deed', a container signal plus the deed it acts on.
explanation.definitionFit: A person showing prejudice against other ethnic groups is a kind of bigot.

clue.text: Red port, endless stuff

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of the word for stuff goes

parts.note: to jam is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: Red wine and port, with some endless stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish red wine from the region of the same name is an example of red.

clue.text: Break line where communion taken

parts.note: a lucky break is a chance

explanation.surface: Breaking the line where people queue for communion.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of a church near the altar is where the sacrament is received.

clue.text: Feeling delighted to eat porridge, ultimate for Scotsman!

indicators.note: the outer word takes in the following letters

parts.note: sent is slang for thrilled or delighted
porridge is British slang for time in prison

indicators.note: the ultimate letter is the last one of the word Scotsman

explanation.surface: Delight at eating porridge, final touch for a Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porridge' looks like breakfast for the Scotsman, but is British slang for a prison sentence, TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotion or attitude is a sentiment, a synonym of feeling.

clue.text: Genie in bottle?

definitions.meaning: a genie is a supernatural being such as one found in a lamp
bottle is British slang for courage or nerve

explanation.surface: A genie trapped in a bottle, as in the old tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' is British slang for nerve; the surface makes it a container holding the genie.
explanation.definitionFit: A genie is a supernatural being, and courage is also called this word, as in showing fighting spirit.

clue.text: Hurdling first of gates, horse high

indicators.note: a horse jumping over a hurdle straddles it, so the horse surrounds the letter

parts.note: a pony is a small horse

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of gates

explanation.surface: A horse clearing the first gate and jumping high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' means smelly, as in high meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat gone off and smelly is said to be high; this British word means stinking.

clue.text: Lacking an edge — with British leading just the same?

definitions.text: Lacking an edge — with British leading just the same?

parts.words: Lacking an edge — with British leading just the same?
parts.note: spectacles or bowls without a rim lack an edge; put B for British in front and the word for a hat without a brim also means lacking an edge

explanation.surface: A query about edgeless things and British leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: Adding B (British) in front gives BRIMLESS, which also means without an edge, so the meaning stays the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Without a rim means having no edge or border, as with frameless glasses.

clue.text: Formidable task in directive from on high?

definitions.meaning: a daunting demand that is hard to meet
a command issued from a great height, read literally as a lofty instruction

explanation.surface: A difficult job set by orders from above.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for an unreasonable demand, also literally an instruction from someone lofty.

clue.text: One seized by staff behind joint, delivering blow

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first in the answer

parts.note: the prefix co- means joint or together, as in co-owner

indicators.note: the walking stick holds the numeral inside it

parts.note: a staff is a cane or stick
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone is grabbed by police behind a dodgy joint as a blow is delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a drug den or a cannabis cigarette, but here it gives CO, as in joint ownership.
explanation.definitionFit: Blow is slang for the powdered stimulant drug from coca leaves.

clue.text: Loamy ground beyond an exceptional thing?

indicators.note: the rearranged soil word comes after the article

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ground means crushed or broken up, so the letters of loamy are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some loamy soil lies past something unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that departs from the rule is an oddity, an exception to the norm.

clue.text: Rubbish tip supporting source of drug

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece goes beneath the other

parts.note: opium comes from the poppy
to cock is to tip or tilt, as a hat

explanation.surface: A rubbish tip propping up where drugs come from.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense or empty talk is rubbish; this is an old informal word for twaddle.

clue.text: Unfortunately, it's my canon that's affected devotion

indicators.note: things gone unfortunately have gone wrong, so the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A grumble that one's own cleric has a showy, insincere piety.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretence of holiness or religious virtue is a smug, put-on piety.

clue.text: Dawn about right for love

indicators.note: the name of the dawn goddess goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: Eos is the Greek goddess of the dawn

explanation.surface: Dawn breaks and it is the right moment for love.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of love and desire, also used for sexual passion itself.

clue.text: Sweet lump rolled over on to sweetheart

indicators.note: the lump word is turned over so it reads backwards

parts.note: a clod is a lump of earth
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: A lump of something rolled onto one's darling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is read as the heart of 'sweet', its central E.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical term for playing sweetly and softly, also used for a dessert wine.

clue.text: Bomb drawing wind up

parts.note: a doodle is an idle drawing
to wind someone up is to annoy or bug them

explanation.surface: A drawing of a bomb meant to provoke.
explanation.walkthrough: The V-1 flying bomb used against Britain in 1944 was nicknamed this.
explanation.definitionFit: The German V-1 flying bomb of the Second World War was given this nickname.

clue.text: Fish on boat repelled by the water

indicators.note: in an across answer, the fish placed on the boat comes after it
pushed back, so the boat word is read in reverse

parts.note: a sloop is a single-masted sailing boat
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A fish landing on a boat and being driven off it.
explanation.definitionFit: The area next to a swimming pool is right beside the water.

clue.text: Drink angered a drunk after round

indicators.note: the shuffled letters follow the round letter

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: drunk suggests something mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man angered by a drunk after buying a round.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizzy citrus soft drink made with fruit juice is a type of drink.

clue.text: Superficial film screened by Universal

indicators.note: hidden behind a screen, so the film title sits inside the other word

parts.note: cosmic means relating to the whole universe
E.T. is the Spielberg film about an alien

explanation.surface: A shallow film shown by the Universal studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Universal' and 'screened' suggest the film studio and cinemas; it is really COSMIC, holding ET.
explanation.definitionFit: Changes that touch only the surface appearance, not the substance, are only skin-deep.

clue.text: Relocate speed of fighter?

parts.note: the MiG is a Russian fighter jet
speed is a rate of movement

explanation.surface: Asking about a fighter jet's speed when moving location.
explanation.definitionFit: To move to live elsewhere, like birds flying south, is to relocate.

clue.text: Warning, a politician has ignored me

indicators.note: leaving something out, so the pronoun is dropped from the politician

parts.note: a Member of Parliament is a politician
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complaining that a politician has not paid them any attention.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle traffic light colour signals caution before red.

clue.text: Rustic in poor family saving a little money

indicators.note: keeping something safe inside, so the outer words hold the coin

parts.note: bum means of poor quality
kin are family
P is a penny, a small British coin

explanation.surface: A country person in a poor family putting aside small sums.
explanation.definitionFit: A clumsy country person is a yokel, and rustic as a noun means the same.

clue.text: Mention item chained, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: to give a product or event a promotional mention
a bath or sink stopper often hangs on a little chain

explanation.surface: Talking about something kept on a chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug is a promotional mention and also the stopper on a chain for a bath.

clue.text: Game, something cured by champion

parts.note: to champion a cause is to back it
gammon is cured ham

explanation.surface: Game meat cured and supplied by a winner.
explanation.walkthrough: GAMMON is cured ham, common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A board game for two players moving pieces by dice rolls.

clue.text: Silver alloy

definitions.meaning: silver here means money or coins; British slang for money
copper and zinc make this yellow alloy

explanation.surface: Silver as a metal alloy.
explanation.definitionFit: Northern British slang for cash, and also the copper-zinc mixture metal.

clue.text: Start in the theatre?

definitions.meaning: present on a stage or film set

explanation.surface: Beginning a career in theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The beginning of something, and read as two words, being on the stage set.

clue.text: Patriarch, a racing driver once losing heart

indicators.note: the middle letter of the driver's surname is taken away

parts.note: Jack Brabham was an Australian Formula One world champion

explanation.surface: An elder statesman who was once a racing driver, now lacking spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical father of the Hebrew nation is the first of the patriarchs.

clue.text: Fool, as in cards

indicators.note: the little word goes inside the cards

parts.note: jacks are court cards
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone playing the fool as if at a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey stands in for a stupid person, so the word is an insult for an idiot.

clue.text: Horse boxes as slippery

indicators.note: encloses as in a box, so the horse holds the little word

parts.note: a grey is a horse of that colour
taken as written

explanation.surface: A horse boxing, as though on slippery ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' looks like fighting or horseboxes but means encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: Something coated in oil or fat is slick and hard to grip.

clue.text: Strip cut in seed

indicators.note: cut short, so the final letter of the comic title is removed

parts.note: Peanuts is Charles Schulz's comic strip

explanation.surface: A strip cut out of a seed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip' is the comic strip Peanuts, shortened by 'cut'.
explanation.definitionFit: The groundnut is botanically a legume's seed eaten as a nut.
